title: world protocol — fleet components
description: The population that moves through a world: robot classes and the cohorts that mint robots, carrier pools and the carriers they mint. A cohort and a pool are generators in the same sense a tiled region is, which is what makes one damaged robot or one curated pre-fill speakable without a second mechanism. Mirrors the crate module of the same name.

robot_class.title: robot class
robot_class.description: A kind of robot, distinguished by configuration as well as model: two robots on one chassis with different end effectors are two classes, because what they can carry differs. Who made it and who rebranded it ride in `lineage` — a rebrand is a party and a role, not a join key into another system or source (SPEC §10, §10.1).

role.description: What this class does in the operation. `htm` and `vtm` are the values in use; the field is deliberately open, because a human operator is a future role rather than a new mechanism.

locomotion.description: How the class gets about: `floor` drives on cell_grids, `ladder` climbs the racking and needs no cells beneath it. Absent reads as `floor` — the exception is the one that has to be declared (SPEC §5).

configuration.description: What distinguishes this build of the model — the end effector, the carrier fitment.

carries.description: The carrier kinds this class can take.

height.description: Overall height, checked against the lowest level of any rack whose footprint a cell_grid admitting this class crosses (SPEC §7).

native_frame.description: The vendor frame this class's own software speaks in.

cohort.title: cohort
cohort.description: N robots of one class plus an assignment policy; a generator of individually addressable robot entities (SPEC §10).

assignment.title: assignment
assignment.description: Where a cohort's robots may work. `hard` means they never leave the listed entities; anything else leaves them free (SPEC §7 — the validator warns when a hard assignment sends a class somewhere it cannot go).

kind.description: How binding the assignment is. `hard` and `free` are the values in use; the reader treats anything that is not `hard` as free, so this is not closed.

to.description: The sectors or regions a hard assignment confines the robots to.

robot.title: robot
robot.description: One robot: which class it is, which cohort minted it, and where it may work. Derived by a cohort or declared by hand, with the same standing either way (SPEC §10).

index.description: Which of the cohort's robots this is, zero-based.

carrier_pool.title: carrier pool
carrier_pool.description: A population of carriers of one type, all carrying one permanent designation, placed by one rule; a generator of individually addressable carrier entities (SPEC §10).

designation.title: designation
designation.description: Which side of the operation a carrier belongs to, permanently — a per-carrier fact rather than a per-type one, which is the anti-starvation ruling (SPEC §10).

placement.title: placement
placement.description: Where a pool's carriers start. The rule names the scheme — a sector, storage spread across the site, named slots — and the fields the scheme needs ride alongside it, which is why this object is not closed (SPEC §10).

kind.description: Which placement scheme applies. `sector` and `distributed_storage` are in use; the third scheme SPEC §10 names, placement into named slots, has no spelling pinned yet, so this is not closed.

carrier.title: carrier
carrier.description: One carrier: its type, the pool that minted it, its permanent designation and where it sits. Derived by a pool or declared by hand, with the same standing either way (SPEC §10).

index.description: Which of the pool's carriers this is, zero-based.
